outlines.56: Overtime: A copies B raised red card, not knowing it marks attendance, then sends B to challenge overtime. Club: A copies crossed booking as protest but B cancelled; B demands public signature. Both need retained work access.
outlines.57: Barbecue: A copies chef tall hat as executive distinction; B says paper hat keeps hair out, then needs A serving. Dinner: A copies folded tall place card as reserved-title signal; B says spill shield and offers a menu cover for title.
outlines.58: Workshop: A copies B checked columns as votes but checks mean costs verified; B offers hybrid. Election: A copies ribbon pinned to bag as faction declaration but B merely holds spare; B asks alternating display.
outlines.59: Office: A copies B desk tap as attention signal, but B testing wobble; A asks increasingly burdensome box positioning to test compliance. Window: A copies raised curtain as team signal, but B needs light; cold makes new coat burden.
outlines.60: Hall: A copies caretaker reversed key ring as handover but B finding taxi key; A asks public referral of dance decision. Meeting: A copies turning chair as procedure but B avoids glare; B must name A as next budget decision-maker.
